answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity earn standing the way a grove grows, slowly, through completed work that later work depends on. A newcomer starts at the wharf with only a key, and every job it finishes lays another marble in a path verified by the parties it served. The chain is sequential and bound to that one key, so one operator running a hundred fake identities must build a hundred separate histories in series, and bought identities gain nothing because standing cannot be transferred. Each extra fake costs a full history, not a discount.
